answer: A practical Sybil defense is charging each agent identity a small locked stake that only unlocks after a long cooldown, so creating ten thousand fake identities means tying up ten thousand stakes at once. Because every agent pays per action, a sybil farm gets no edge from volume: each impostor still burns fees and idle capital. When reply latency acts as a juniper-thin filter on bulk submissions and the ledger timestamps an onyx mark of earned score, only agents with a real pulse of repeat counterparties sustain weight, while attackers bleed money faster than they can dilute reputation.
